newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Killings, thefts, rapes on rise in Buenos Aires.
newsitem.headline: Killings, thefts, rapes on rise in Buenos Aires.

text.p: Crime in Argentina's capital shot up by 41.4 percent between 1994-96, according to a police report issued on Sunday.

Judges and policemen interviewed by the Clarin newspaper said there were entire neighbourhoods that police hardly dared to enter, including the infamous Fort Apache west of the capital, where armed gangs usually engage in street battles.
But gang violence serves a purpose, commissioner Abel Miqueleiz, chief of security of the Buenos Aires police told Clarin. "It produces an ecological cleansing of the criminal fauna," he said.
Hold-ups shot up by 44 percent to 65,700 cases, the report showed. Killings and rapes grew at a slower pace.

The report follows an opinion poll published last week showing that one of four Buenos Aires dwellers was robbed or mugged in the past six months. Two-thirds of respondents said they dreaded walking in the streets of a city that just a few years ago had a good safety reputation.
High crime rates in the Buenos Aires province go hand in hand with police corruption.

Late last year Buenos Aires governor Eduardo Duhalde, tipped as the most likely successor to President Carlos Menem in the 1999 election, vowed to clean up the act of the 48,000-strong provincial police, the country's largest security force.
He has received at least two threats since he launched a purge of corrupt agents from the force. His government is expected to release this week the names of 500 officers to be summarily fired.

Investigations into the brutal killing of a news photographer last December near Duhalde's summer house led to the arrest of several Buenos Aires policemen and to speculation it might have been a warning for the governor to halt the purge.
